mainTopic: Starting things before שבת (or פסח) that continue on their own: dealings with a גוי, travel, sieges, laundry, presses, and processes that run by themselves
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about selling חמץ to a גוי: רבי יהודה forbids selling כותח during the thirty days before פסח, because it lasts a long time. A new ברייתא allows putting food before a dog or a גוי in the courtyard on שבת, even if they carry it out. The גמרא explains why the גוי case is taught separately. Further ברייתות forbid renting utensils to a גוי or sending letters with him on ערב שבת, and the גמרא clarifies when a letter may still be sent: with a fixed price, or where the town has a set mail house. Other ברייתות forbid setting sail or starting a siege fewer than three days before שבת, with some exceptions. The גמרא then turns to the משנה: white clothes went to the launderer earlier than colored ones, and אביי puts this to practical use. It explains why בית שמאי did not forbid loading the presses: that work would not bring a חטאת even on שבת. Finally, it traces the rule that a process running by itself on שבת is permitted to רבי ישמעאל, quoting a משנה whose second opinion, from רבי עקיבא, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: כותח may not be sold thirty days before פסח
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא about selling חמץ to a גוי. This line is the closing opinion of רבי יהודה, whose name appears at the very end of the previous amud: כותח and all similar dips may not be sold to a גוי during the thirty days before פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Babylonian כותח, and all kinds of כותח, may not be sold to a gentile during the thirty days before פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list from a ברייתא about selling חמץ to a גוי before פסח. Here it adds a special rule for כותח, a dip made with bread crumbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier part of the ברייתא, בית שמאי allow selling חמץ to a גוי only if he will finish it before פסח, and בית הלל allow selling it as long as one may still eat it. רבי יהודה adds a stricter rule for כותח. People eat only a little of it at a time, so it lasts a long time, and he therefore forbids selling it thirty days ahead.

keyTerms.meaning: A dip or relish made with bread crumbs (חמץ), whey and salt

phrases.english: Babylonian kutach and all kinds of kutach
phrases.notes: A dip containing leavened bread crumbs.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to sell [to a gentile] thirty days
phrases.notes: Because it lasts a long time.

phrases.english: before Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּתָּח הַבַּבְלִי וְכׇל מִינֵי כּוּתָּח אָסוּר לִמְכּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא that began on the previous amud, about selling חמץ to a גוי before פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: כותח may not be sold to a גוי during the thirty days before פסח, because it lasts a long time.

steps.title: Food may be put before a dog on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: you may put food in front of a dog in the courtyard on שבת. If the dog carries it out, you do not need to chase after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We may put food in front of a dog in the courtyard. If the dog took it and went out, we do not need to bother with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It says you may feed a dog in your courtyard on שבת, even though the dog might carry the food out into the public domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dog has no obligation to keep שבת, and the person did nothing wrong by feeding it. So if the dog carries the food out, the owner does not have to stop it. This fits the theme of the סוגיא: we are not responsible for what happens afterward on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא
We do not need to bother with him or stop him

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We may put food before the dog in the courtyard.
If it took it and went out —
we do not need to bother with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נוֹתְנִין מְזוֹנוֹת לִפְנֵי הַכֶּלֶב בֶּחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on a related theme: what happens after something leaves our control.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may feed a dog in the courtyard on שבת, and you are not responsible if it carries the food out.

steps.title: The same rule applies to a gentile
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: in the same way, you may put food before a גוי in the courtyard. If he carries it out, you do not need to stop him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly: We may put food in front of a gentile in the courtyard. If he took it and went out, we do not need to bother with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second case that works like the first: feeding a גוי in your courtyard on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי is not commanded to keep שבת, so his carrying the food out is not a problem for the Jew who fed him. The ruling is word-for-word the same as the dog case. That sameness sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He took it and went out

phrases.english: Similarly:
We may put food before the gentile in the courtyard.
If he took it and went out — we do not need to bother with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ: נוֹתְנִין מְזוֹנוֹת לִפְנֵי הַגּוֹי בֶּחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case to the dog ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may feed a גוי in the courtyard on שבת, and you are not responsible if he carries the food out.

steps.title: Why repeat the same rule for the gentile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs the גוי case at all, since it seems identical to the dog case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this as well? This is the same as that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for repeating itself. If the dog case is already taught, the גוי case seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither a dog nor a גוי is commanded to keep שבת. So the reasoning behind both cases looks the same. The assumption is that a ברייתא does not waste words, so there must be a reason for the second case.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this too?
This is the same as that

phrases.english: Why do I need this as well?
This is the same as that!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי, הַיְינוּ הָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the case in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second case of the ברייתא (feeding a גוי)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule and its reasoning are identical to the dog case, so the second case looks unnecessary.

steps.title: Responsibility for feeding makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: Answer: we might have thought feeding the dog is allowed only because its owner is responsible for feeding it, and that feeding a גוי is not allowed. So the ברייתא teaches that the גוי case is also permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: this one (the dog) is his responsibility, and this one (the gentile) is not his responsibility. So the ברייתא teaches us that both are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the extra case is needed. It shows a real difference between the dog and the גוי that might have led to a stricter ruling for the גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding your own dog is your duty, so it makes sense to allow it even with some risk. Feeding a גוי is not your duty, so we might have said you should not take the risk that he will carry the food out on שבת. The ברייתא teaches that even so, it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

phrases.english: You might have said:
this one is his responsibility,
phrases.notes: The dog: its owner must feed it.

phrases.english: and this one is not his responsibility —
phrases.notes: The גוי: he has no duty to feed him.

phrases.english: so it teaches us [that it is permitted].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא: הַאי רְמֵי עֲלֵיהּ, וְהַאי לָא רְמֵי עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows that the second case is needed to block a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Feeding a גוי would be forbidden, since you have no duty to feed him and should not take the risk.
steps.terutzMaskana: Feeding a גוי is permitted too, even though you have no duty to feed him.
steps.whatToRemember: Dog and גוי are both allowed to be fed in the courtyard on שבת. The גוי case is taught separately because we might have thought it was stricter, since we have no duty to feed him.

steps.title: No renting utensils to a gentile on Friday
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: you may not rent your utensils to a גוי on ערב שבת, but on Wednesday or Thursday it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may not rent his utensils to a gentile on ערב שבת. On Wednesday and Thursday it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about renting your utensils to a גוי close to שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you rent out utensils on Friday, the גוי will clearly use them on שבת. It then looks as if the Jew is being paid for work done on שבת. When the rental starts on Wednesday or Thursday, it is not obviously linked to שבת, so it is allowed.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person may not rent his utensils to a gentile
on Shabbat eve,
on the fourth and fifth [days] it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא יַשְׂכִּיר אָדָם כֵּלָיו לְגוֹי בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on a related topic: dealings with a גוי before שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Renting utensils to a גוי is forbidden on Friday and permitted on Wednesday or Thursday.

steps.title: No sending letters with a gentile on Friday
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: you may not send letters with a גוי on ערב שבת, but on Wednesday or Thursday it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, we do not send letters in the hand of a gentile on ערב שבת. On Wednesday and Thursday it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A parallel case to the utensils: giving a גוי a letter to deliver right before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A letter given on Friday will be carried by the גוי on שבת, and he is acting as the Jew's messenger. If it is given on Wednesday or Thursday, there is enough time for delivery, so it is not tied to שבת and is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: In the hand of a non-Jew, as a messenger

phrases.english: Similarly,
we do not send letters in the hand of a gentile
on Shabbat eve,
on the fourth and fifth [days] — it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, אֵין מְשַׁלְּחִין אִיגְּרוֹת בְּיַד גּוֹי בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case to the utensils rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sending a letter with a גוי is forbidden on Friday and permitted on Wednesday or Thursday.

steps.title: רבי יוסי never had a letter in a gentile's hand
steps.stepSummary: A report about רבי יוסי הכהן (some say רבי יוסי החסיד): a letter in his handwriting was never found in the hand of a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי יוסי הכהן, and some say about רבי יוסי החסיד, that his handwriting was never found in the hand of a gentile.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a story about a pious sage who was stricter than the law, as an example of extra care.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By law, sending a letter with a גוי on Wednesday or Thursday is fine. But this sage never sent letters with a גוי at all, so that his letter would never be carried on שבת. This is מידת חסידות (extra piety), not the basic הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: His handwriting, meaning a letter he wrote

steps.confusionAlert: This story does not change the הלכה. Sending letters on Wednesday or Thursday is still permitted; רבי יוסי simply went beyond the law.
steps.whatToRemember: Renting utensils or sending letters with a גוי is forbidden on ערב שבת and allowed earlier in the week. A pious person may avoid it completely.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Yosei the Kohen,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ עַל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הֶחָסִיד,
phrases.english: and some say about Rabbi Yosei the Chasid,
that his handwriting was never found
in the hand of a gentile, ever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows extra piety that goes beyond the Wednesday and Thursday permission of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי never sent letters with a גוי at all, as an act of extra piety.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between the basic הלכה and מידת חסידות, which is a frequent theme when the גמרא reports a sage's personal practice.

steps.title: A letter may be sent with a gentile on Friday only for a set price
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not send a letter with a גוי on ערב שבת unless a set price is fixed. בית שמאי and בית הלל then disagree about how much time must be left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: You may not send a letter with a גוי on Friday unless you fix a set price for him. בית שמאי say: only if there is enough time for him to reach the house. בית הלל say: enough time for him to reach the house next to the city wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about giving a letter to a גוי to deliver on ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a set price is fixed, the גוי works for his own pay, so whatever he does on שבת is his own business and not the Jew's. בית שמאי require enough time to reach the destination house before שבת. בית הלל require only enough time to reach the first house by the wall of the destination city.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixes a set price for him (a set fee for the whole job)
The house next to the city wall (the first house of the destination city)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְשַׁלְּחִין אִיגֶּרֶת בְּיַד גּוֹי עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: One may not send a letter in the hand of a gentile on Friday,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן קוֹצֵץ לוֹ דָּמִים.
phrases.english: unless he fixes a set price for him.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְבֵיתוֹ,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: enough time for him to reach the house,
phrases.notes: The house the letter is being sent to (the destination).

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say:
enough time for him to reach the house next to the wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְשַׁלְּחִין אִיגֶּרֶת בְּיַד גּוֹי עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the earlier ruling (step 7) that letters may not be sent with a גוי on ערב שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A letter may be sent with a גוי on ערב שבת only for a set price. The time limit is disputed: to the destination house (בית שמאי) or to the house by the city wall (בית הלל).

steps.title: If a price was fixed, why does timing matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: once a set price was fixed, why should it matter whether the גוי arrives before שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't he fix a set price?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the time limits seem pointless if a price was already fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A set price makes the גוי's work his own, so it should not matter when he travels. So why would בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about how much time is needed?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that…? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't he fix a set price?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא קָצַץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the internal logic of the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The מחלוקת of בית שמאי and בית הלל in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fixed price already removes the problem, so a time requirement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רב ששת: the dispute is about a case with no fixed price
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל refers to a case where no price was fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This is what the ברייתא means. If he did not fix a price, בית שמאי say he may send it only if there is time to reach the house, and בית הלל say only if there is time to reach the house next to the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת re-reads the ברייתא so the time limits apply only when no price was set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a fixed price, there is no time limit at all. Without a fixed price, the letter may still be sent, but only if there is enough time to arrive before שבת. The two schools disagree only about how far 'arrive' means.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (re-reading the text)
An אמורא who explains the ברייתא

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: this is what it is saying:
And if he did not fix a price —

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְבֵיתוֹ,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: only if he can reach the house,
and Beit Hillel say:
only if he can reach the house next to the wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the text (הכי קאמר): the second half refers to a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The time limits apply even when a price was fixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The time limits apply only when no price was fixed.

steps.title: But the first part forbids sending without a price
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the ברייתא's first line says you may not send without a fixed price, so how can the second line permit it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said in the first part, 'one may not send' unless a price is fixed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב ששת's reading now makes the ברייתא contradict itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening line forbids sending without a fixed price. רב ששת's reading allows sending without a fixed price if there is enough time, so the two halves seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But you said… (pointing to a contradiction)
The first part of the text

phrases.english: But you said in the first part: one may not send?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ רֵישָׁא אֵין מְשַׁלְּחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's reading from step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause forbids sending without a fixed price, but the explanation permits it. That is a contradiction within the same ברייתא.

steps.title: It depends on whether the town has a set mail house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two halves describe different towns: one with a fixed mail house and one without.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This (sending without a price is allowed) is where there is a fixed mail house in town. That (a price is required) is where there is no fixed mail house in town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the ברייתא into two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where a regular mail house exists, the letter goes through a known system, so a fixed price is not needed, only enough time. Where there is no mail house, the גוי is clearly working for the Jew, so a fixed price is required.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
This case… and that case… (splitting into two situations)

steps.whatToRemember: Fixed price: always allowed. No fixed price: allowed only where there is a set mail house and enough time (per בית שמאי or בית הלל). No price and no mail house: forbidden.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where there is a fixed mail house in the town,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דְּלָא קְבִיעַ בֵּי דַוָּאר בְּמָתָא.
phrases.english: and that is where there is no fixed mail house in the town.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דִּקְבִיעַ בֵּי דַוָּאר בְּמָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בכך הא בכך)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves of the ברייתא are about the same situation and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is about a town with no mail house, and the second is about a town with one.

steps.title: No setting sail within three days of Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: one may not set sail on a ship fewer than three days before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: You may not set sail on a ship fewer than three days before שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about beginning a ship journey shortly before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another case of starting something before שבת that continues into שבת. The first days at sea are unsettling and would ruin עונג שבת. Others explain that it looks like doing מלאכה on שבת.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not set sail on a ship
fewer than three days before Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַפְלִיגִין בִּסְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: ship travel before שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not set sail fewer than three days before שבת.

steps.title: The ban applies only to optional trips, not מצוה trips
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the rule to an optional trip. A trip for a מצוה is allowed even close to שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When was this said? For an optional trip. But for a מצוה, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא narrows its own rule by explaining when it applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three-day ban covers only a דבר הרשות (an optional matter, like business or pleasure). For a דבר מצוה, one may set sail even within three days of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: When was this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
For an optional matter;
but for a מצוה matter —
it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — לִדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three-day ban applies only to optional trips. Trips for a מצוה are permitted.

steps.title: Must he stipulate that the ship stop for שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that even on a מצוה trip one must stipulate with the captain to stop on שבת, even if he does not actually stop. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says no stipulation is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he makes a condition with him (the captain) that the ship will stop for שבת, even though it does not actually stop. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: he does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא records a מחלוקת about whether the traveler must formally ask the גוי captain to stop on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי requires the condition, even if the captain ignores it, so the Jew is not seen as wanting the ship to sail on שבת. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that no condition is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes an agreement / stipulates with him
On condition to rest (stop the ship on שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: 'And he does not rest' does not cancel the condition. רבי says the condition must be made even though, in practice, the captain will not actually stop.

phrases.english: And he stipulates with him on condition to rest,
and even if he does not rest —
these are the words of Rebbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He need not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפוֹסֵק עִמּוֹ עַל מְנָת לִשְׁבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition (disputed) to the permitted case from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי requires a stipulation with the captain to stop on שבת. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not.

steps.title: A short trip from צור to צידון is allowed even on Friday
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by allowing the short sea trip from צור to צידון even on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from צור to צידון, it is permitted even on Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a final exception for a very short trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trip from צור to צידון is short enough to finish before שבת. So none of the concerns apply, and one may set sail even on ערב שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Sailing: forbidden within three days of שבת for an optional trip. Allowed for a מצוה (with a disputed stipulation). A short trip like צור to צידון is fine even on ערב שבת.

phrases.english: And from Tyre to Sidon —
even on Friday it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִצּוֹר לְצִידֹן — אֲפִילּוּ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final exception to the three-day rule of step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A short voyage like צור to צידון may begin even on ערב שבת.

steps.title: No siege fewer than three days before שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not begin a siege on non-Jewish cities fewer than three days before שבת. If the siege already began, it does not need to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not besiege cities of non-Jews less than three days before שבת. But if they already started, they do not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about starting a siege close to שבת. It follows the same pattern as the ship rule in the previous steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting up a siege takes heavy work in the first days, so starting it right before שבת could lead to חילול שבת. The three-day buffer lets that heavy work be finished beforehand. Once the siege is underway, it is not interrupted for שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is another example in the סוגיא of a rule about starting something before שבת that keeps going into שבת.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צָרִין עַל עֲיָירוֹת שֶׁל גּוֹיִם
phrases.english: One may not besiege cities of non-Jews
less than three days before Shabbat.
And if they began, they do not stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין צָרִין עַל עֲיָירוֹת שֶׁל גּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel ברייתא to the ship rule: a three-day buffer before שבת for an ongoing activity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not start a siege less than three days before שבת; once begun, it continues.

steps.title: שמאי's verse: the siege continues even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמאי derives from the פסוק "עד רדתה" (until it falls) that the siege goes on even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so שמאי used to say: "Until it falls" — even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a פסוק as the source for why a siege does not stop for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says to keep up the siege "until it falls" and names no break for שבת. שמאי reads this as permission to continue on שבת. This supports the second half of the ברייתא: once begun, the siege does not stop.

phrases.english: And so Shammai would say:
"Until it falls" — even on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק source for continuing the siege on שבת.
steps.raayaObject: That a siege already begun continues on שבת.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's household and laundry before שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and brings a ברייתא from רבי צדוק: white clothes went to the launderer three days before שבת, colored clothes even on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: They were accustomed, etc. It was taught: רבי צדוק said, this was the custom of רבן גמליאל's house: they gave white clothes to the launderer three days before שבת, and colored clothes even on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line in the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains it more fully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only mentioned white clothes. רבי צדוק adds that colored clothes could be given even on ערב שבת. The difference is about how long the non-Jewish launderer would need, so he would not be working on the Jew's clothes on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
They were accustomed, etc.
It was taught: Rabbi Tzadok said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: This was the custom of the house of Rabban Gamliel:
that they would give white garments to the launderer
three days before Shabbat,
and colored ones even on Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: נוֹהֲגִין הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה, the laundry custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: White clothes go to the launderer three days before שבת; colored clothes may go even on ערב שבת.

steps.title: White clothes are harder to wash than colored ones
steps.stepSummary: From the different deadlines, we learn that white clothes take more work to wash than colored clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: From their words we learned that white clothes are harder to wash than colored ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a practical fact from the custom it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would white clothes need three days while colored clothes need only one? Because white clothes take longer to get clean, since every stain shows. The time limits reveal how hard each job is.

keyTerms.meaning: and from their words we learned

phrases.english: And from their words we learned

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַלְּבָנִים קָשִׁים לְכַבְּסָן יוֹתֵר מִן הַצְּבוּעִין.
phrases.english: that white ones are harder to wash than colored ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדִּבְרֵיהֶם לָמַדְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רבי צדוק's ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: White garments are harder to launder than colored garments.

steps.title: אביי argues with the launderer about the price
steps.stepSummary: The launderer asked אביי for the white-garment price to wash a colored garment. אביי answered that the חכמים had already taught that colored garments are easier.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was giving a colored garment to a launderer. He asked him: How much do you want for it? He said: The same as for a white one. אביי said to him: The חכמים already got ahead of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where אביי puts the lesson from the last step to practical use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The launderer tried to charge the higher price. אביי pointed to the ברייתא, which shows that colored clothes take less work. So the price should be lower.

phrases.english: Abaye was giving
a certain colored garment to the launderer.
He said to him: How much do you want for it?
He said to him: As for a white one.
He said to him: The Rabbis already preceded you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה יָהֵיב לֵיהּ הַהוּא מָנָא דִצְבִיעָא לְקַצָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Practical application of the inference that white clothes are harder to wash.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing a colored garment should cost less than washing a white one.

steps.title: אביי's advice: measure the garment before and after
steps.stepSummary: אביי advises measuring a garment when giving it to the launderer and when taking it back, so you can tell if it was stretched or shrunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Someone who gives a garment to a launderer should give it by measure and take it back by measure. If it is longer, he ruined it by stretching it. If it is shorter, he ruined it by shrinking it.
steps.whatsHappening: Staying on the launderer topic, אביי gives a practical tip for protecting yourself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Measuring creates a record. Any change in length shows damage. Longer means it was overstretched, and shorter means it shrank, so the launderer is responsible either way.
steps.whatToRemember: The laundry section: white clothes need more time and cost more than colored clothes, and אביי advises measuring garments given to a launderer.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דְּיָהֵיב מָנָא לְקַצָּרָא,
phrases.english: Abaye said: One who gives a garment to the launderer,
should give it to him by measure
and take it from him by measure.
For if it is longer, he caused a loss by stretching it.
And if it is shorter, he caused a loss by shrinking it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דְּיָהֵיב מָנָא לְקַצָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further advice from אביי on the launderer topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measure a garment when giving it to a launderer and again when taking it back.

steps.title: Why did בית שמאי allow loading the presses?
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה that both sides agree one may load the presses, the גמרא asks why בית שמאי forbade all the other cases but not these.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And these and those agree that one may load," etc. What is different about all the other cases, where בית שמאי made a decree, and what is different about the beams of the olive press and the wine press, where they did not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and asks a question to set up the next step's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי usually forbid starting a task before שבת if it keeps going on שבת. Yet even they allow loading the presses right before שבת. The גמרא wants the rule that separates the two kinds of cases.

keyTerms.meaning: and these and those (בית שמאי and בית הלל) agree
circles (of grapes) in the wine press

phrases.english: And these and those agree that one may load, etc.:
What is different about all of them
that Beit Shammai decreed against them,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא קוֹרוֹת בֵּית הַבַּד וְעִיגּוּלֵי הַגַּת
phrases.english: and what is different about the olive-press beams and the wine-press circles
that they did not decree?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא כּוּלְּהוּ דִּגְזַרוּ בְּהוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה about the presses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that explains when בית שמאי made a decree and when they did not.

steps.title: בית שמאי only decreed where שבת work would bring a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי decreed only on tasks that would bring a חטאת if done on שבת. Loading the presses would not bring a חטאת even on שבת, so they did not decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those cases, where doing them on שבת makes a person liable for a חטאת, בית שמאי forbade on ערב שבת at nightfall. The olive-press beams and wine-press circles, where doing them on שבת does not make one liable for a חטאת, they did not forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the principle behind בית שמאי's decrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dividing line is how serious the act would be on שבת itself. For full מלאכות that carry a חטאת, בית שמאי added a safeguard even before שבת. Loading the presses carries no חטאת even on שבת, so there was no need for that extra safeguard.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's ערב שבת decrees apply only to activities that would bring a חטאת if done on שבת. Loading the presses does not, so it is allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean בית שמאי treat the presses as having nothing to do with שבת rules. It only explains why their special ערב שבת decree does not reach this case.

phrases.english: Those, where if one does them on Shabbat
he is liable for a sin-offering,

phrases.aramaic: גְּזַרוּ בְּהוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת עִם חֲשֵׁכָה.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai decreed against them on Shabbat eve at nightfall.
The olive-press beams and wine-press circles,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי עָבֵיד לְהוּ בְּשַׁבָּת לָא מִיחַיַּיב חַטָּאת —
phrases.english: where if one does them on Shabbat he is not liable for a sin-offering,
they did not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנָךְ דְּאִי עָבֵיד לְהוּ בְּשַׁבָּת מִיחַיַּיב חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי decreed only where the act on שבת would bring a חטאת. Loading the presses would not, so it was not decreed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The scope of בית שמאי's decree is limited to activities that would bring a חטאת on שבת.

steps.title: Who is the source for allowing processes that run on their own?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that anything that happens by itself, without a person acting on שבת, is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that anything that comes about on its own is perfectly fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא is the source for the idea that a process running by itself on שבת is allowed. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא allowed loading the presses before שבת even though liquid keeps flowing out on שבת. Now it wants to know which named authority holds this principle. The point is to tie the rule to a specific תנא, so we know it is not simply obvious or agreed by everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא? This asks which Sage holds a certain view.
On its own, by itself, without anyone actively doing it.
It is perfectly fine, it is permitted.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna
that anything that comes about on its own,
phrases.notes: For example, liquid that keeps flowing from produce under a press that was loaded before שבת.

phrases.english: is perfectly fine?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דְּכֹל מִידֵּי דְּאָתֵי מִמֵּילָא שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why בית שמאי did not decree against loading the presses, the גמרא now looks for the תנא behind the general principle that a self-running process is permitted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which named תנא holds that a process that continues by itself on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: It is רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers that the principle follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: It is רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gives the answer: this principle follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer names one specific תנא, which suggests that others may disagree. The proof for this answer comes in the next step, from a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question.
It is רבי ישמעאל, meaning this view follows him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
phrases.notes: The words in brackets fix the wording: read 'ברבי' instead of 'בר'.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yishmael,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The principle that a self-running process is permitted follows רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה of crushed garlic, grapes, and stalks
steps.stepSummary: The proof comes from a משנה: if someone crushed garlic, unripe grapes, or wheat stalks before שבת, רבי ישמעאל says he may finish after dark. רבי עקיבא's view starts here and continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: garlic, unripe grapes, and wheat stalks that he crushed while it was still day. רבי ישמעאל says: he may finish after it gets dark. And רבי עקיבא says...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that רבי ישמעאל is the source. This passage ends right as רבי עקיבא's opposing opinion begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crushing was done before שבת. After dark, the liquid keeps seeping out from the crushed produce by itself. רבי ישמעאל allows finishing the process, so he holds that what happens on its own on שבת is fine. רבי עקיבא's view, given on the next amud, will show the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה. This introduces a quote from a משנה.
Unripe ears or stalks of grain.
While it was still day, before שבת began.
After it gets dark, once שבת has begun.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל does not allow crushing on שבת itself. The crushing was done before שבת. He only allows finishing the process, while the liquid keeps coming out by itself.

phrases.english: as we learned: the garlic, the unripe grapes, and the stalks
that he crushed while it was still day,
Rabbi Yishmael says: he may finish after it gets dark,
phrases.notes: The liquid keeps seeping out by itself on שבת.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva says:
phrases.notes: His view continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן הַשּׁוּם וְהַבּוֹסֶר וְהַמְּלִילוֹת שֶׁרִסְּקָן מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה that supports the answer of step 27.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the self-running process principle follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about garlic, unripe grapes, and stalks crushed before שבת, where רבי ישמעאל says one may finish after dark.
